correctness.rationale: On b+c=3a+1/2 with positive a,b,c and neither b-a nor c-a a nonpositive integer, the published sector-uniform asymptotic has exactly matching z^(-2a) powers. After nonzero normalization, G(z)=R+cos(z-πa)+(d/2z)sin(z-πa)+O((1+exp|Im z|)/|z|²) on the closed right half-plane away from a compact disk. For |R|≠1, the model roots form two separated simple 2π-periodic strings. Away from fixed disjoint root disks the model has a uniform lower bound c exp|Im z| (from periodicity on bounded-height strips and exponential growth at large height); the error is smaller for sufficiently large |z|. Rouché on each far-right disk counts exactly one zero, hence simple; no other large right-half-plane zeros occur. A simple-root Taylor expansion yields d/(2w)+O(n^-2). Real coefficients and one root per conjugation-invariant disk give the real-tail case |R|<1; disks disjoint from the real axis yield off-axis height arcosh|R| for |R|>1. Evenness handles the left side; bounded zeros and |R|=1 are excluded. Independently recomputed d=-3/16 at (a,b,c)=(1/4,1/8,9/8); finite parameter probes are not the infinite proof.
